figures.title: Which failure modes does the design make plausible?
figures.caption: MASQ Stage 2: each MAST failure mode, grouped by the Stage-1 dimension it is mapped to. The LLM classifies the design's protection (explicit guardrail / prompt-only / architectural); code applies the paper's rule (Low / Mid / High). Paper columns are the authors' Table 2; '(!)' marks anticipated ≠ observed.

figures.title: Stage 3: did the anticipated failures show up in real traces?
figures.caption: A tiny ChatDev-shaped chat chain was screened (Stage 2) and then run on small coding tasks; an LLM annotated each trace (T1…) against MAST. '(!)' uses a matching rule that reproduces the paper's flags: Low ≤ 2/30, Mid 2/30–8/30, High ≥ 8/30.

figures.title: When the agents say it's verified, is it?
figures.caption: Hidden unit tests (never shown to the agents) on each trace's final code, with whether the reviewer approved and the tester passed it.
